name: GameCube Controller Adapter (Wii U / Switch): Full
notes: The Wii U GameCube adapter, WUP-028, as Dolphin, Slippi and SDL read it through libusb: one USB device with four controller ports. The descriptors are a real adapter's byte for byte: USB 2.00, full speed, bMaxPacketSize0 8, bcdDevice 1.00, strings Nintendo, WUP-028 and 15/07/2014, one HID interface with interrupt IN 0x81 of 37 bytes and interrupt OUT 0x02 of 5 bytes at 8 ms, and the 214-byte report descriptor of gamecube-adapter-hid. Every unit carries the serial 15/07/2014, so a second adapter gets a Windows instance named after its port. The adapter sends nothing until a host writes 0x13. From then on each host poll gets report 0x21: the report ID and nine bytes per port, a status byte (0x04 rumble power, 0x10 wired, 0x22 a WaveBird communicating, 0x20 a WaveBird that is not: Dolphin, SDL and ToadKing's driver read 0x20 as a connected WaveBird, and Nintendont alone as an empty port), two button bytes, the sticks, and the analog L and R. 0x11 sets each port's motor, 0x12 reads the origins, 0x14 stops the reports and 0x15 stops the adapter until a port reset. A reply that finds another still waiting is dropped. A SET_REPORT(Output) is one command, its whole data stage, less a leading report ID that matches wValue's, as tinyusb drops it before loopj's firmware reads the command. GET_REPORT answers the requested report ID alone, as loopj's firmware does. SET_PROTOCOL succeeds. extendedReport.ports and protocol describe all of it as data. Windows' HID parser rejects the report descriptor, so a real adapter has no HID collection on Windows, and HMController.BindWinUsb binds WinUSB to this device alone. HMController.Ports takes input per port, and SubmitState goes to port 1. docs/design/v1.13.0.md has the sources.

layout.perPortLayout: A GameCube controller: main stick, C-stick, analog L and R with their clicks, Z, Start, A, B, X, Y and the D-pad. The report descriptor declares byte arrays under Game Controls, as the real adapter's does, so it names no axes or buttons, and extendedReport.ports maps each port's nine bytes.
